title: Renoviction by-law report and 400 Westwood rezoning
subtitle: Annual zoning update, new legal position, heritage designations, e-billing review, pet-friendly city update and Muslim women's group funding request
overview: Council approved a rezoning for 400 Westwood Drive to allow townhouses, after changes made since committee. Changes included paired driveways and a wider side yard next to the neighbouring home to the south. A neighbour and a neighbourhood association delegate opposed it over tree loss and a shared retaining wall. Council also approved the annual zoning by-law update and a new legal services position to help meet provincial deadlines for development applications.

On evictions for renovations, many tenants and advocates asked Council to pass a by-law. Staff said a report is already due in June 2025. Council directed staff to return on February 10, 2025 on whether that report can be brought forward {{vote:m2}}. Staff cautioned that provincial authority is unclear and an earlier report would have less data.

Council also asked staff to study making new customers default to e-billing and to review incentives {{vote:m10}}. It approved heritage designation notices for two properties, adopted a phasing brief for 1001 King Street East, and appointed a member to the Committee of Adjustment. Delegates also asked for operational funding for an anti-hate reporting service and for more pet-friendly city properties.

decisions.detail: Council approved the zoning change for 400 Westwood Drive in the form set out in the addendum report, with an added clause saying no further public notice is required {{vote:m1}}.
Staff must report on February 10, 2025 on whether the earlier-requested renoviction by-law report, including a review of other municipalities' by-laws, can be expedited ahead of June 2025.

decisions.item: Annual zoning by-law update and legal position
decisions.detail: Council approved the city-initiated updates to Zoning By-laws 85-1 and 2019-051 and a new Legal Services Administrator position to support timely review of development applications.

Staff will assess grandfathering current paper-bill customers, options for new customers, incentives and communication through e-bills, and report to the Finance and Corporate Services committee in the second quarter of 2025.
The Clerk will publish a Notice of Intention to Designate 69 Agnes Street under the Ontario Heritage Act.

decisions.item: 80-86 Union Boulevard / 571 York Street heritage notice
decisions.detail: The Clerk will publish a Notice of Intention to Designate 80-86 Union Boulevard / 571 York Street as having cultural heritage value.
Council adopted the phasing brief and directed staff to report back before final site plan approval of any vertical tower phasing projects received before December 31, 2026.
Maria Melo was appointed to the Committee of Adjustment for a term ending November 14, 2026, or until a successor is appointed.

debate: On 400 Westwood, the applicant's planner said the side yard beside the southern neighbour grew from 2.5 to 4 metres and driveways were paired. Three of four trees on that side would likely be removed, one for disease. Staff said later consent and building permit stages would check grading and drainage.

The southern neighbour argued that removing the mature trees would damage a stone retaining wall and put their home at risk, and asked for a modest tree protection buffer. A neighbourhood association delegate objected to rezoning from Res 1 to Res 4 in a mature treed area. Staff said they made a mapping change so the tree protection area stays Res 1.

On renovictions, tenants and advocates described harassment, rising rents and fear of homelessness. They said other cities have passed by-laws and asked Council to act sooner. Several councillors urged faster action, including delaying other work such as the fireworks by-law review.

Staff and other councillors urged caution. They said only one comparable by-law is in force, Hamilton's, with no applications yet. The province holds primary authority, and a by-law might need many new staff. They wanted an enforceable by-law rather than one that raises false hope, and committed to continued advocacy to the province.
A delegate from the Coalition of Muslim Women said its anti-hate service has lost project funding and needs operational support. The Mayor said staff could review other grants it might apply for.
